result.title: Track4D: Representing Dense 3D Tracking for Video Diffusion Models
result.summary: We study how to repurpose video diffusion models (VDMs), pretrained on millions of videos, for dense 3D point tracking, where training data is scarce. Doing so is non-trivial, as it requires representing 3D tracks as video-like signals that may lie outside the natural-video distribution on which the VDM was trained. We thus systematically assess the effectiveness of two such video representations. The first, Residual 3D Tracking Video (RTV), encodes per-pixel 3D offsets relative to a query frame and allows recovery of 3D trajectories directly from the generated video. The second, Normalized Coordinate Map Video (NCMV), labels each pixel with a canonical coordinate invariant through time. This is closer to a natural video and easier for the VDM to learn, but requires additional post-processing with an off-the-shelf 2D tracker to recover 3D tracks. RTV tracks more accurately, while NCMV shows that a VDM can generate dense correspondence as a video. We instantiate both representations with LoRA adaptation of a frozen Wan backbone, conditioned on point maps from an off-the-shelf 3D reconstructor as a geometric scaffold. Trained with a single dynamic 3D tracking dataset, Track4D achieves competitive zero-shot tracking on four real and synthetic benchmarks. A regression readout that bypasses the video VAE and uses additional training data brings further improvement, demonstrating the potential of this direction for dense 3D tracking. We hope our analysis will inspire future work that leverages VDM priors for dense 3D tracking and 4D reconstruction. Project page: https://nirvanalan.github.io/projects/track4d

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何复用预训练视频扩散模型做稠密 3D 点跟踪，系统比较两种把 3D 轨迹编码成视频信号的表示（逐像素 3D 偏移的 RTV、时间不变的归一化坐标图 NCMV），并以冻结 Wan 加 LoRA、点图作为几何条件，另设绕过 VAE 的回归读出头。
AI.relevance_reason: 原文对「表示是否贴近自然视频」与精度、需否额外后处理的取舍，以及绕过 VAE 的回归读出，可供核查生成式 latent 是否保留几何任务必要信息、latent 内容能否被有效读出与使用这一 LVR 问题，属可能的方法借鉴线索，非已验证结论。
